records.reason: m61 at 5/1 PE provides a donor-containing condition response point complementary to the same molecule at 1/1 PE in this batch, helping separate solvent-ratio effects from donor-scaffold behavior.
A simple aliphatic ketone at 2/1 DCM is an ordinary low-complexity onset and completion anchor for calibrating carbonyl effects against delayed aromatic carbonyl rows.
The longer-chain aryl ketone at 2/1 DCM tests how added hydrophobic chain length changes retention relative to simpler ketone controls without introducing donors or basic centers.
A low-ratio anisyl ketone in PE supplies a weak-solvent baseline for aromatic ketone and ether interactions before stronger-ratio response curves are learned.
This nitrile-containing ketone is an acceptor-rich but donor-free control, useful for distinguishing generic acceptor count from the severe aromatic adsorption regime.
An iodophenol under strong PE-rich elution tests whether a donor plus heavy atom remains compact or develops the scaffold-specific donor tail seen in fused aromatic alcohol families.
A flexible aryl ketone at 10/1 DCM probes solvent response in an intermediate carbonyl scaffold between ordinary acetophenones and fused or multi-carbonyl failures.
This high-ratio benzophenone-like row targets endpoint-specific completion behavior in a two-aromatic carbonyl scaffold and can test whether V2 broadening exceeds V1 movement.
A dibrominated aromatic aldehyde at weak DCM conditions supplies a heavy-atom carbonyl anchor, guarding against transferring delayed carbonyl corrections to weakly interacting structures.
An aromatic acrylate in PE expands ester coverage and tests whether conjugation and flexible ester geometry produce a distinct onset or completion response.
A phenolic aldehyde at strong PE-rich conditions probes donor-assisted aldehyde retention and separates phenol effects from donor-free aldehyde behavior.
Chloroiodobenzene at 2/1 DCM is a compact heavy-halogen calibration anchor with no hydrogen-bond donor or acceptor.
A brominated phenolic aldehyde at high-ratio DCM tests combined donor and heavy-atom effects in a structurally distinct aldehyde scaffold.
The halogenated benzaldehyde at 2/1 DCM provides a donor-free aldehyde control for comparison with phenolic aldehydes and delayed carbonyl families.
A fused ketone at 1/1 DCM tests whether fused-ring geometry alone produces delayed completion, providing a carbocyclic control for polar fused structures.
This simple allylic bromide supplies a low-interaction, high-ratio PE anchor that helps stabilize calibration outside polar and carbonyl failure regions.
A small aromatic diketone at 10/1 DCM probes whether multiple carbonyls predict a local V2 tail while retaining a relatively compact molecular framework.
A phenolic aromatic ester tests donor placement and intramolecular interaction effects against neutral ester controls and other donor-containing aromatic rows.
Fused anisole at 10/1 DCM is a donor-free fused aromatic control for separating ring fusion and ether effects from donor-driven tails.
A methoxyacetophenone at 10/1 DCM samples an acceptor-rich but nonbasic ketone regime and supports endpoint-specific interpolation across aromatic ketones.
The second m61 condition forms a same-molecule PE ratio contrast with the 5/1 condition, directly testing whether donor effects change onset and completion together.
A heavy biphenyl bromide at high PE ratio provides a nonpolar aromatic anchor for testing whether strong solvent shifts remain compact in the absence of silica-binding groups.
Acetophenone at 5/1 PE is a simple aromatic ketone reference for separating ordinary solvent response from delayed fused or multi-carbonyl behavior.
A methylbenzaldehyde at 5/1 PE adds a compact donor-free aldehyde control and tests transfer from ketones to aldehydes.
An anisole-like aromatic ester at weak DCM conditions supplies a neutral ester baseline for comparison with phenolic and amino ester families.
The second m9 condition provides a same-scaffold DCM ratio contrast for a weakly interacting bromobiphenyl, useful for learning solvent response without polar functional groups.
A tertiary benzylic alcohol at weak DCM conditions tests whether flexible donor-containing structures remain compact when the donor is sterically shielded.
The second m127 condition forms a low-to-moderate PE ratio contrast within an anisyl ketone family, helping learn onset and completion slopes separately.
A low-volume weak-PE m9 anchor probes loading sensitivity in a nonpolar heavy aromatic and helps prevent polar-tail corrections from spreading globally.
A high-ratio bromoacetophenone-like row tests whether a halogen plus one carbonyl remains a compact control or develops a ratio-dependent aromatic ketone tail.
A halogenated anisole at 1/1 DCM expands neutral ether and heavy-atom calibration at moderate loading, complementing nonpolar anchors.
A chlorinated aromatic ester at 20/1 DCM probes strong-solvent ester response while remaining donor-free, helping distinguish ester-specific tails from donor and basic effects.

hypotheses.content: Compact hydrophobic and weakly interacting rows are necessary calibration anchors because severe tails in polar or adsorption-prone families do not justify global endpoint inflation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These controls constrain baseline V1 and V2 calibration and reduce the risk that corrections for severe tails degrade ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do weakly interacting heavy-atom and fused aromatic structures remain compact across PE and DCM ratio changes?

hypotheses.content: Large V2 completion tails are localized to scaffold-condition-loading neighborhoods and require endpoint-specific corrections rather than generic polarity or carbonyl offsets.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local V2 corrections address the dominant historical errors while preserving compact-row accuracy.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched carbonyl and ester controls preserve family-specific completion tails across solvent ratios?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount, loading-solvent volume, and mobile-phase ratio interact non-smoothly, with V2 sometimes changing much more than V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Same-molecule and same-family contrasts expose interactions that structure-only similarity cannot learn reliably.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed scaffold, do ratio and loading shifts move onset and completion together or mainly create a V2 tail?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing aromatic structures have scaffold-specific retention tails; donor count alone does not determine whether the response is compact or delayed.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Donor-family controls teach attachment geometry, steric environment, and flexibility effects instead of imposing a global HBD correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor-containing aromatic scaffolds switch from compact elution to delayed completion as ratio or loading changes?

hypotheses.content: Some aromatic ketone, ester, and donor-free aromatic families show threshold-like onset changes with solvent strength, with V1 and V2 not necessarily scaling proportionally.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Condition curves teach separate onset and completion responses and improve interpolation between sparse ratio levels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do simple ketone, ester, and aldehyde families show reproducible onset thresholds while completion remains locally calibrated?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback reinforced localized endpoint behavior. m177 was compact at 50/1 and 100 ul but had a very large V2 at 20/1 and 150 ul, weakening any monotone ratio-only rule. m125 and m199 likewise showed strong condition-dependent completion tails. Severe fused alcohol outcomes extended donor-family failures beyond simple alcohols, while compact heavy-halogen outcomes supported retaining ordinary calibration anchors. The batch therefore emphasizes same-molecule ratio contrasts, neutral controls around carbonyl and ester families, donor geometry, loading interactions, and compact hydrophobic references.
batch_rationale: The 32 legal candidates form several local experiments rather than a single functional-group sweep. Same-scaffold contrasts for m61, m9, and m127 teach condition response; ketones, aldehydes, esters, diketones, and fused carbonyls cover distinct endpoint regimes; donor and phenolic rows test scaffold-specific adsorption; and heavy-halogen and nonpolar rows constrain baseline calibration. This combination repairs failure-prone endpoint regions while supplying compact controls that help keep corrections local and improve generalization across the Row-distribution.
